To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we find the time-lag response to be symmetric about zero velocity for the three symmetric line profiles, (2) the time-lag ratios for optical emission lines are consistent with the predictions of Korista & Goud (2004, ApJ, 606, 151), and (3) we find the virial masses of the central black hole to be generally consistent within the measurement uncertainties.
we have measured the virial masses of the central black holes in 10 AGNs and have found that the masses are consistent with the virial masses derived from the broad Hβ time lags.

we have measured the masses of 12 nearby active galactic nuclei (AGNs), and that we find that the masses derived from the broad Hβ line and those derived from the Hα, He I, and He II lines are consistent with each other within the uncertainties.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the determination of black hole mass in AGNs.
the measurement and interpretation of the broad emission-line response to continuum variations in AGNs.
the study of the physical properties of the broad line emitting gas in active galactic nuclei.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
reverberation mapping has proven its utility for measuring black-hole masses, and that it is a viable tool for determining masses for black holes with masses up to 107 M ☉.
the time-lag measurements and the derived black hole masses are generally consistent with expectations, but that the data are not of sufficient quality or quantity to make any firm conclusions.
reverberation mapping has now been shown to work for the Hβ, Hα, and Hγ lines and for He I and He II.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
reverberation mapping of AGN broad lines has matured to the point where it can be used for black hole mass determinations in many AGNs.

the reverberation mass estimates for the black holes in the sample are consistent with each other and with those derived from the broad Hβ response and that the photoionization calculations of Korista & Gead are broadly consistent with the data.

we find the masses of the supermassive black holes in the AGNs in the sample to be consistent with those expected from the relationship between the mass of the central black hole and the velocity dispersion in the host galaxy bulge.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the optical recombination line time lags are useful in the measurement of black hole masses and that the optical recombining line time-lag ratios can be used to estimate the black hole mass when the time lag of Hβ is known.
the time lags are consistent with the predictions of photoionization calculations, but the time lag of the Hα line is significantly longer than predicted.
we can measure the masses of the central black holes in these Seyfert galaxies to within 10% or better, which is a substantial improvement over the previous estimates.
